content: The following is a professional summary of the content provided: 1. A systematic review and meta-analysis published in JNCI Cancer Spectrum in 2019 examined the quality of life in cancer survivors. 2. This study, published in Sports Medicine in 2018, analyzed randomized trials and provided insights into the efficacy of these exercise modalities. 3. Liu Y and colleagues explored the relationship between resistance exercise intensity and improvements in HbA1c and insulin levels in patients with type 2 diabetes. Their systematic review and meta-analysis, published in International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health in 2019, highlighted the benefits of resistance training for glycemic control. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behavior, emphasizing the importance of exercise for various health outcomes. 5. Ibeneme SC and colleagues reviewed the effects of physical exercise on inflammatory biomarkers and cardiopulmonary function in patients living with HIV. Their systematic review and meta-analysis, published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2019, demonstrated the positive impact of exercise on these parameters. 6. Poto R and colleagues conducted a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the effects of resistance training in HIV-infected patients. Published in Journal of Sports Science in 2016, the study highlighted the benefits of resistance training for this population. 7. Pedro RE and colleagues systematically reviewed the effects of physical training on individuals with HIV-associated lipodystrophy syndrome. Their findings, published in Journal of Sports Medicine and Physical Fitness in 2017, underscored the role of exercise in managing this condition. 8. O’Brien KK and colleagues assessed the effectiveness of aerobic exercise for adults living with HIV in a systematic review and meta-analysis using the Cochrane Collaboration protocol. Published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2016, the study confirmed the benefits of aerobic exercise for this population. 9. Heissel A and colleagues conducted a meta-analysis on the effects of exercise on depression and anxiety in individuals living with HIV. Their findings, published in Journal of Psychosomatic Research in 2019, demonstrated significant mental health benefits. 10. Sluik D and colleagues investigated the relationship between physical activity and mortality in individuals with diabetes mellitus. Their prospective study and meta-analysis, published in Archives of Internal Medicine in 2012, highlighted the protective effects of physical activity on mortality risk. 11. Kodama S and colleagues performed a meta-analysis to examine the association between physical activity and the risk of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular disease in patients with diabetes. Published in Diabetes Care in 2013, the study emphasized the importance of physical activity in reducing these risks. 12. Sadarangani KP and colleagues analyzed data from 10 population-based cohorts in Great Britain to assess the impact of physical activity on all-cause and cardiovascular disease mortality in diabetic adults. Their pooled analysis, published in Diabetes Care in 2014, reinforced the benefits of physical activity. 13. Qiu S and colleagues conducted a meta-analysis on the effects of aerobic interval training on cardiometabolic health in patients with type 2 diabetes. Published in Frontiers in Physiology in 2017, the study highlighted the advantages of this exercise modality. 14. Campbell E and colleagues systematically reviewed the use of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) for individuals with multiple sclerosis. Their findings, published in Multiple Sclerosis and Related Disorders in 2018, demonstrated the potential benefits of HIIT for this population. 15. Manca A and colleagues conducted a meta-analytic and scoping study on the effects of strength training in individuals with multiple sclerosis. Published in Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research in 2019, the study highlighted the role of strength training in improving physical function. 16. Patterson KK and colleagues systematically reviewed the use of dance as a rehabilitation tool for balance and gait in adults with neurological conditions other than Parkinson’s disease. Their findings, published in Heliyon in 2018, demonstrated the effectiveness of dance-based interventions. 17. Alphonsus KB and colleagues reviewed the effects of exercise, yoga, and physiotherapy on the quality of life in individuals with multiple sclerosis. Their systematic review and meta-analysis, published in Complementary Therapies in Medicine in 2019, highlighted the positive impact of these interventions. 18. Dos Santos Delabary M and colleagues systematically reviewed the effects of dance practice on functional mobility, motor symptoms, and quality of life in individuals with Parkinson’s disease. Their findings, published in Aging Clinical and Experimental Research in 2018, emphasized the benefits of dance for this population. 19. Cugusi L and colleagues reviewed the use of Nordic walking for managing Parkinson’s disease. Their systematic review, published in PM&R in 2017, demonstrated the effectiveness of this exercise modality. 20. Stuckenschneider T and colleagues systematically reviewed the effects of different exercise modes on domain-specific cognitive function in patients with Parkinson’s disease. Their findings, published in Journal of Parkinson’s Disease in 2019, highlighted the cognitive benefits of exercise. 21. Stubbs B and colleagues provided guidance on physical activity as a treatment for severe mental illness. Their meta-review, supported by the European Psychiatric Association (EPA) and published in European Psychiatry in 2018, emphasized the role of exercise in mental health management. 22. Krogh J and colleagues systematically reviewed the effects of exercise on patients with major depression. Their meta-analysis, published in BMJ Open in 2017, confirmed the antidepressant effects of physical activity. 23. Firth J and colleagues systematically reviewed the impact of aerobic exercise on cognitive functioning in individuals with schizophrenia. Their findings, published in Schizophrenia Bulletin in 2017, demonstrated significant cognitive improvements. 24. Maiano C and colleagues systematically reviewed exercise interventions aimed at improving balance in young individuals with intellectual disabilities. Their findings, published in Developmental Medicine and Child Neurology in 2018, highlighted the benefits of such interventions. 25. Maiano C and colleagues also reviewed the effects of exercise interventions on balance in children and adolescents with Down syndrome. Their findings, published in Physical Therapy in 2019, demonstrated the positive impact of these interventions. 26. Ashdown-Franks G and colleagues conducted a meta-review on the benefits of exercise for mental and substance use disorders. Their findings, published in Sports Medicine in 2019, emphasized the role of exercise in improving neuropsychiatric and cognitive outcomes. 27. Ding D and colleagues analyzed the global economic burden of physical inactivity in relation to major non-communicable diseases. Their findings, published in The Lancet in 2016, underscored the significant economic impact of inactivity. 28. Ceccini M and Bull F discussed strategies for promoting physical activity in the context of public health. Their work was included in The Economic Case for Public Health Action. 29. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a guidance note in 2019 on the prevention and control of non-communicable diseases, emphasizing the importance of investment in physical activity. 30. The WHO also released a technical package in 2018, titled ACTIVE, aimed at increasing physical activity globally. 31. The WHO conducted a global survey in 2019 to assess national capacities for preventing and controlling non-communicable diseases, with findings published in 2020. 32. The WHO Steering Group, composed of experts in physical activity, adolescent health, aging, mental health, injury prevention, cancer, pregnancy, and surveillance, developed the scope and recommendations for the guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behavior.
